fields.detailed services: WIC
fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Montezuma County
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable
fields.hours of operation: Monday - Wednesday, 7:30 a.m. - 5:30 p.m.; Thursday, 7 a.m. - 5:30 p.m.

title: Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) — Montrose County Department of Human Services — 1845 S Townsend Ave - Montrose County
summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program designed to help qualifying low-income households pay for a portion of their winter home heating costs. LEAP is available and applications are accepted from November 1st - April 30th and may only be used once per heating season. LEAP payments are given directly to the heating fuel vendor or placed on a EBT card to pay for heating sources, such as:    Wood   Coal  Propane   Heat billed on a shared meter

fields.organization name: Montrose County Department of Human Services
fields.detailed services: Heating Fuel Payment Assistance
fields.service summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program designed to help qualifying low-income households pay for a portion of their winter home heating costs. LEAP is available and applications are accepted from November 1st - April 30th and may only be used once per heating season. LEAP payments are given directly to the heating fuel vendor or placed on a EBT card to pay for heating sources, such as:    Wood   Coal  Propane   Heat billed on a shared meter
fields.eligibility: Applicants must:    Be a permanent legal resident of the United States and Colorado, or have a household member that is a US citizen   Pay home heating costs to a heating provider, fuel dealer, or landlord as part of rent   Have a maximum household income that falls within the guidelines below       'Household” means people who live with you and for whom you are financially responsible. Household Size Monthly Gross Income for the 2024-2025 Season                 60% of State Median Income    1 - $3,382  2 - $4,423  3 - $5,464  4 - $6,505  5 - $7,545  6 - $8,569  7 - $8,781  8 - $8,977  Each Additional Person $195    Area Served: Montrose County
fields.access method: Apply online. Visit the website to download a paper application and drop off at the local DHS office or mail/email to the county to process. Call to request a mailed paper application, to apply over the phone, or for more information.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Proof of citizenship if born outside of the US   Proof of all monthly household income    If self-employed, receipts for all expenses claimed on profit and loss statement   Copy of most recent heating bill or recent rent receipt, if heat is included with rent
fields.hours of operation: November 1st - April 30th (Application Open); Monday - Friday, 8 a.m. - 5 p.m. (Administrative Hours)

summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes

fields.detailed services: WIC
fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Montrose County
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable

title: Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) — Morgan County Department of Human Services — 800 E Beaver Ave - Morgan County
summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program that helps eligible Colorado households with a portion of their winter home heating costs. Applications are accepted each year from November 1st - April 30th. The benefit does not cover the full cost of heating and is offered once per season. title: Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) — Northeast Colorado Health Department — 700 Columbine St - Logan County
summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes

fields.detailed services: WIC
fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Statewide
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable

summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Breastfeeding information  Support groups  Classes

fields.detailed services: WIC
fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Breastfeeding information  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Statewide
fields.access method: Call to schedule an appointment or for more information.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable

If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Statewide
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable

summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes

fields.detailed services: WIC
fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Ouray County
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable

fields.detailed services: Heating Fuel Payment Assistance
fields.service summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program designed to help qualifying low-income households pay for a portion of their winter home heating costs. LEAP is available and applications are accepted from November 1st - April 30th and may only be used once per heating season. LEAP payments are given directly to the heating fuel vendor or placed on a EBT card to pay for heating sources, such as:    Wood   Coal   Propane   Heat billed on a shared meter
fields.eligibility: Applicants must:    Be a permanent legal resident of the United States and Colorado, or have a household member that is a US citizen   Pay home heating costs to a heating provider, fuel dealer, or landlord as part of rent   Have a maximum household income that falls within the guidelines below    'Household” means people who live with you and for whom you are financially responsible. Household Size Monthly Gross Income for the 2022-2023 Season                 60% of State Median Income    1 - $3,081  2 - $4,030  3 - $4,978  4 - $5,926  5 - $6,875  6 - $7,823  7 - $8,001  8 - $8,179  Each Additional Person $177          Area Served: Park County
fields.access method: Visit website to apply online. A paper application can also be downloaded online to be dropped off at the local human services office or mail/email to the county to process. Call to request a mailed paper application, to apply over the phone, or for more information.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Proof of citizenship if born outside of the US   Proof of all monthly household income    If self-employed, receipts for all expenses claimed on profit and loss statement   Copy of most recent heating bill or recent rent receipt, if heat is included with rent
